Floor still 18/92; the whole residual is the tail. Found jump.c:1764 (bare-goto exit reproduces target's beqz sense), KILLED every exit-spelling/label-order variant (8 forms, byte-identical 19/93), pr

Permuter broke the three-session plateau: honest distance 18 -> 7 at target's exact 91 instructions, via three independently measured levers (mask constant staged through the live loop counter, mask t

Session-4's distance-7 form is a DIFFERENT PROGRAM (its pointer re-base makes arg5 = tbl[i0+i1], target passes tbl[i1]); the honest faithful floor is 8/91, the arg block is now closed at the source-or

Forensics: the arg block's SHAPE is decided at expand (inline argument => load emitted straight into $a3 last; named local => load at the statement) and its ORDER by sched1's INSN_PRIORITY + dependenc

frontier.hypothesis: The whole argument-block residual is now ONE quantity: the idx_1494[0] address chain must outrank the D_800A11D5 chain in sched1's INSN_PRIORITY so its lbu is issued first and its load last, giving it the block-long live range that lands it in $a0.
frontier.mechanism: rank_for_schedule (sched.c:2399) sorts the ready list by INSN_PRIORITY = longest path to the block end, then by the dependence class relative to last_scheduled_insn (sched.c:2412-2449), then by INSN_LUID (2452-2455, proven inert here). The two chains are isomorphic — lbu -> sll -> addu -> lw <hard arg reg> -> call — so they tie on priority and the class rule breaks the tie toward D_800A11D5. Only a DAG change can separate them.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the semantically faithful DAG changes that lengthen the idx_1494[0] chain's path to the call or shorten the D_800A11D5 chain's, and measure each: (a) reading D_800A11D5 through the tbl_11dc pointer or another already-live pointer instead of as a bare symbol_ref (removes/adds a link); (b) declaring idx_1494 or the tables with a different element width so the address chain gains or loses the sll; (c) hoisting the D_800A11D5 byte read out of the block entirely (it is loop-invariant) so its chain no longer competes. Screen with tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s6/score.py and confirm the DAG effect in the .sched order with s6/order.py <tag> sched — do NOT re-try statement reordering, which is proven inert.

frontier.hypothesis: The 14/91 inline-arg4 family, not the 8/91 named-arg4 candidate, is the correct chassis for the argument block, so a permuter campaign or hand sweep seeded there can reach a lower true floor even though its starting score is higher.
frontier.mechanism: Session 6 proved the 8/91 form's fourth argument has the wrong expand-time RTL (a standalone load coalesced onto $a3 early) while the inline form has target's (`set (reg a3) (mem ...)` emitted last). Score is therefore a misleading ranking between the two basins, exactly as sessions 4 and 5 found the permuter's weighted score to be for this function. The inline family's best member is n4 at 13/91.
